operational_definition: pH-dependent cell death triggered by alkaline conditions and characterized by the involvement of nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) pathways and carbonic anhydrase 9 (CA9) downregulation.
operational_definition_complement: A pH-dependent form of regulated cell death triggered by alkaline conditions, demarcated by NF-kB pathway activation and carbonic anhydrase 9 downregulation.
core_mechanism: pH-dependent death under alkaline conditions; NF-kB/CA9-dependent
overlaps: pH-dependent cell death, overlaps with other stress-induced cell deaths.
provenance_note: Retain as lesser-known distinct pathway; require form-specific assay criteria. [5] OD: AI-extracted from PDF corpus A (GPT-4o), human-validated.

operational_definition: A contextual cell-death process triggered by ammonia, demarcated by cytoplasmic vacuolation, and detoxified via arginase-mediated urea production with L-glutamine protection.
overlaps: vacuolar/necrotic features
provenance_note: Inducer-defined label; do not assume a unique execution mechanism.

operational_definition: Specific variant of intrinsic apoptosis initiated by the loss of integrin-dependent anchorage
operational_definition_complement: Form of apoptosis induced by detachment from the extracellular matrix, critical for preventing metastasis.
core_mechanism: Apoptosis triggered by ECM detachment
overlaps: Form of apoptosis induced by detachment from the extracellular matrix, critical for preventing metastasis.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: Specific variant of intrinsic apoptosis initiated by the loss of integrin-dependent anchorage
provenance_note: Keep as detachment-context death; do not assume a single execution mechanism.

operational_definition: A syncretic cell death variant sharing features of apoptosis and necrosis, triggered by high-dose mitochondrial insult and demarcated by incomplete execution of the apoptotic program, with intracellular ATP as a determinant.
overlaps: apoptosis + necrosis
provenance_note: Do not aggregate automatically with apoptosis or necrosis.

operational_definition: Programmed cell death characterized by cell shrinkage, chromatin condensation, and DNA fragmentation. Autonomous cell lysis without causing inflammation, involved in life and death balance of tumor cells.
operational_definition_complement: A form of programmed cell death demarcated by cell shrinkage, chromatin condensation and DNA fragmentation, executed as autonomous cell lysis without inflammation.
core_mechanism: Programmed cell death with shrinkage, chromatin condensation, DNA fragmentation
overlaps: Interconnected with necroptosis and pyroptosis through shared molecular pathways and caspase activation.
provenance_note: Keep as parent; roll intrinsic and extrinsic apoptosis upward only for broad reporting. [2, 3]

operational_definition: Specific variant of RCD initiated by perturbations of the extracellular microenvironment detected by plasma membrane receptors, propagated by CASP8 and precipitated by executioner caspases, mainly CASP3
operational_definition_complement: A subtype of apoptosis initiated by death-receptor oligomerization, propagated by FADD and caspase-8.
overlaps: subtype of Apoptosis
galluzzi_nccd_definition: Specific variant of RCD initiated by perturbations of the extracellular microenvironment detected by plasma membrane receptors, propagated by CASP8 and precipitated by executioner caspases, mainly CASP3
provenance_note: Child of apoptosis. [2]

operational_definition: Type of RCD initiated by perturbations of the extracellular or intracellular microenvironment, demarcated by MOMP, and precipitated by executioner caspases, mainly CASP3
operational_definition_complement: A subtype of apoptosis demarcated by mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization and regulated by Bcl-2/Bcl-xL.
overlaps: subtype of Apoptosis
galluzzi_nccd_definition: Type of RCD initiated by perturbations of the extracellular or intracellular microenvironment, demarcated by MOMP, and precipitated by executioner caspases, mainly CASP3
provenance_note: Child of apoptosis. [2]

operational_definition: Self-digestion process where cells degrade their own components through lysosomes. Phagocytic biological process essential for maintaining cell function and homeostasis.
operational_definition_complement: A lysosomal self-digestion process whereby cells degrade their own components, essential for cellular function and homeostasis.
core_mechanism: Lysosomal self-digestion and cellular recycling
overlaps: Dual role; can lead to autophagic cell death or survival through cellular recycling.
provenance_note: Do not treat generic autophagy as death; map death claims to autophagy-dependent cell death when evidence meets that definition. [2]

operational_definition: A form of RCD that mechanistically depends on the autophagic machinery (or components thereof)
operational_definition_complement: A form of regulated cell death that depends on the autophagic machinery, demarcated by autophagosome accumulation and blockade of basal autophagic flux.
overlaps: autophagy; 'autophagic cell death' predates
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A form of RCD that mechanistically depends on the autophagic machinery (or components thereof)
provenance_note: Use for death that depends on the autophagic machinery; keep distinct from generic autophagy. [2]

operational_definition: A specific instance of autophagy-dependent cell death that critically relies on the plasma membrane Na + /K + -ATPase
operational_definition_complement: A subtype of autophagy-dependent cell death, dependent on the Na+/K+-ATPase pump.
core_mechanism: Autophagy-dependent death requiring Na/K-ATPase
overlaps: Subtype of autophagy, relies on Na+/K+-ATPase.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A specific instance of autophagy-dependent cell death that critically relies on the plasma membrane Na + /K + -ATPase
provenance_note: Retain separately but link to autophagy-dependent cell death; do not automatically inherit evidence.

operational_definition: Irreversible loss of proliferative potential associated with specific morphological and biochemical features, including the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Cellular senescence does not constitute a form of RCD
operational_definition_complement: Stable cell cycle arrest where cells remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate.
core_mechanism: Stable cell cycle arrest with metabolic activity; SASP secretion
overlaps: Stable cell cycle arrest where cells remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: Irreversible loss of proliferative potential associated with specific morphological and biochemical features, including the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Cellular senescence does not constitute a form of RCD
provenance_note: Retain for provenance but exclude from a strict death-mechanism heatmap. [2]

operational_definition: A terminal differentiation program of keratinocytes producing the cornified (keratinized) barrier and culminating in a specialized form of programmed cell death.
overlaps: terminal differentiation
provenance_note: Terminal differentiation program; retain as contextual biology, not as a generic RCD mechanism.

operational_definition: Regulated cell death driven by copper accumulation and associated mitochondrial stress.
operational_definition_complement: A form of regulated cell death driven by copper accumulation and associated mitochondrial stress.
core_mechanism: Copper accumulation driving mitochondrial stress
overlaps: Copper-dependent, overlaps with ferroptosis in metal ion dysregulation.
provenance_note: Retain as an emerging mechanism with a dedicated gene-validation review. OD: AI-extracted from PDF corpus A (GPT-4o), human-validated.

operational_definition: Condition in which abnormal expression of SLC7A11 under glucose starvation causes disulfide accumulation and stress leading to cell death.
operational_definition_complement: A form of regulated cell death triggered by disulfide accumulation under glucose starvation, dependent on abnormal SLC7A11 expression.
core_mechanism: SLC7A11-mediated disulfide accumulation under glucose starvation
overlaps: Triggered by disulfide accumulation, overlaps with oxidative stress pathways.
provenance_note: Retain as an emerging distinct form; review definition/version before cross-form comparison. OD: AI-extracted from PDF corpus A (GPT-4o), human-validated.

operational_definition: Mechanism whereby dead cells and fragments thereof are taken up by phagocytes and disposed
operational_definition_complement: Process by which apoptotic or dead cells are removed by phagocytic cells, preventing an inflammatory response.
core_mechanism: Phagocytic clearance of apoptotic/dead cells preventing inflammatory leakage
overlaps: Process by which apoptotic or dead cells are removed by phagocytic cells, preventing an inflammatory response.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: Mechanism whereby dead cells and fragments thereof are taken up by phagocytes and disposed
provenance_note: Phagocytic clearance of dead cells; retain only as a contextual/clearance annotation.

operational_definition: A type of RCD that originates from actomyosin-dependent cell-in-cell internalization (entosis) and is executed by lysosomes
operational_definition_complement: Cell death resulting from one cell being engulfed by another. Form of cell death characterized by the engulfment and killing of one cell by another.
core_mechanism: Cell-in-cell cannibalism; one cell engulfing and killing another
overlaps: Cell-in-cell structure, overlaps with autophagy and lysosome-dependent cell death.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A type of RCD that originates from actomyosin-dependent cell-in-cell internalization (entosis) and is executed by lysosomes
provenance_note: Use entotic cell death as the canonical concept name. [2]

operational_definition: Novel form of cell death reported during the natural turnover of Drosophila gut enterocytes.
operational_definition_complement: A novel form of cell death reported during the natural turnover of gut enterocytes.
core_mechanism: Novel cell death reported in gut enterocyte turnover
overlaps: Novel form of cell death reported during the natural turnover of gut enterocytes.
provenance_note: Retain in a specialized branch; exclude from generic cross-RCD mechanism scoring. OD: AI-extracted from PDF corpus A (GPT-4o), human-validated.

operational_definition: A cell-type-specific form of regulated cell death of erythrocytes, demarcated by cell shrinkage, membrane blebbing, calpain activation and phosphatidylserine exposure, and triggered by oxidative stress via prostaglandin E2/Ca2+ and phospholipase A2/ceramide pathways.
overlaps: PS-exposure clearance (apoptosis/efferocytosis-like)
provenance_note: Erythrocyte-specific programmed death; retain in a cell-type-specific branch.

operational_definition: A form of RCD initiated by oxidative perturbations of the intracellular microenvironment that is under constitutive control by GPX4 and can be inhibited by iron chelators and lipophilic antioxidants
operational_definition_complement: Iron-dependent form of cell death characterized by the accumulation of lipid peroxides. Oxidative and non-apoptotic programmed cell death induced by iron-dependent lipid peroxide injury.
core_mechanism: Iron-dependent lipid peroxide accumulation
overlaps: Iron-dependent, involves oxidative stress; interconnected with other RCDs through shared stress pathways.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A form of RCD initiated by oxidative perturbations of the intracellular microenvironment that is under constitutive control by GPX4 and can be inhibited by iron chelators and lipophilic antioxidants
provenance_note: Retain as an independent core RCD form. [2]

operational_definition: A form of regulated cell death demarcated by cytoplasmic vacuolization with fused-lysosome-associated termination, triggered by Bergeyella cardium infection and inhibited by sodium-channel blockade.
overlaps: lysosome-associated vacuolar death
provenance_note: Retain as supplied; require a source-level operational definition before scoring.

operational_definition: A taxon-specific programmed cell death of plant cells at infection sites, restricting pathogen spread.
overlaps: plant innate-immunity death
provenance_note: Plant immune-response program; retain only in a taxon-aware scope.

operational_definition: A form of RCD that is sufficient to activate an adaptive immune response in immunocompetent hosts
operational_definition_complement: Form of cell death that activates the immune system against dead cell antigens.
core_mechanism: Dying cells expose/release DAMPs activating adaptive immunity
overlaps: Form of cell death that activates the immune system against dead cell antigens.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A form of RCD that is sufficient to activate an adaptive immune response in immunocompetent hosts
provenance_note: Retain independently; its defining feature is immunological consequence rather than a universal upstream mechanism. [2]

operational_definition: A taxon-specific, caspase-independent (ced-3-independent) non-apoptotic developmental cell death of the Caenorhabditis elegans linker cell, demarcated by nuclear crenellation and organelle swelling, and controlled by let-7 and LIN-29.
overlaps: non-apoptotic developmental death
provenance_note: Developmental, taxon-specific label; retain separately.

operational_definition: A lysosome-dependent cell-death subtype demarcated by serpin/SERPINB3-moderated lysosomal membrane permeabilization and cathepsin-L-dependent cytoplasmic proteolysis, executed in the absence of neutralizing endogenous serpin inhibition.
overlaps: subtype of LDCD
provenance_note: Possible lysosome-associated death label; do not merge automatically.

operational_definition: A type of RCD demarcated by primary LMP and precipitated by cathepsins, with optional involvement of MOMP and caspases
operational_definition_complement: A lysosome-dependent cell death demarcated by primary lysosomal membrane permeabilization and cysteine-cathepsin (B/L) proteolysis; a synonym of lysosome-dependent cell death.
overlaps: synonym of LDCD
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A type of RCD demarcated by primary LMP and precipitated by cathepsins, with optional involvement of MOMP and caspases
provenance_note: Potential lexical variant of lysosome-dependent cell death; retain both labels until source-level adjudication. [2]

operational_definition: A type of RCD demarcated by primary LMP and precipitated by cathepsins, with optional involvement of MOMP and caspases
operational_definition_complement: Cell death dependent on the permeabilization of lysosomes and the release of cathepsins.
core_mechanism: Lysosomal permeabilization releasing cathepsins
overlaps: Involves lysosomal enzymes, overlaps with autophagy and apoptosis.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A type of RCD demarcated by primary LMP and precipitated by cathepsins, with optional involvement of MOMP and caspases
provenance_note: Use as canonical label; map lysosomal cell death as a synonym candidate after source-level review. [2]

operational_definition: A regulated non-apoptotic, lysosomal zinc-dependent cell-death process (emerging concept).
overlaps: metalloptosis umbrella
provenance_note: Retain separately; do not automatically merge with lysosome-dependent cell death.

operational_definition: An umbrella term for metal-ion-based regulated cell death, encompassing ferroptosis, cuproptosis, lysozincrosis, manganism, calcicoptosis and necrosis by sodium overload.
key_molecules: metal ions (Fe, Cu, Zn, Mn, Ca, Na)
overlaps: umbrella of metal-RCD forms
provenance_note: Use as a metal-dependent-death umbrella, not a discrete mechanism, pending operational definition.

operational_definition: Unique morphological characteristics involving vacuolization distinct from other forms of cell death.
operational_definition_complement: A form of cell death demarcated by unique vacuolization distinct from other cell death forms.
core_mechanism: Non-apoptotic death with macropinosome-derived vacuoles; Ras/Rac1-driven
overlaps: Characterized by large vacuole formation, overlaps with macropinocytosis and autophagy.
provenance_note: Retain as lesser-known distinct pathway; require form-specific assay criteria. [5]

operational_definition: Involves the opening of a non-selective pore in the inner mitochondrial membrane, leading to loss of membrane potential and cell death.
operational_definition_complement: A trigger event demarcated by opening of a non-selective pore in the inner mitochondrial membrane, leading to loss of membrane potential and cell death.
core_mechanism: Opening of mPTP causing loss of mitochondrial membrane potential
overlaps: Involves the opening of a non-selective pore in the inner mitochondrial membrane, leading to loss of membrane potential and cell death.
provenance_note: Map provisionally to MPT-driven necrosis but preserve original label. [2]

operational_definition: Selective elimination of damaged mitochondria, triggered by mitochondrial permeability transition and oxidative stress.
operational_definition_complement: A mitochondrial quality-control process of selective elimination of damaged mitochondria, triggered by mitochondrial permeability transition and oxidative stress.
core_mechanism: Selective elimination of damaged mitochondria (organelle-level quality control)
overlaps: Selective elimination of damaged mitochondria, overlaps with autophagy and apoptosis.
provenance_note: Retain source label unchanged pending definition and synonym review.

operational_definition: Oncosuppressive mechanism for the control of mitosis-incompetent cells by RCD or cellular senescence. Per se, mitotic catastrophe does not constitute a form or RCD
operational_definition_complement: Cell death resulting from abnormal mitosis, often due to mitotic failure and genomic instability.
core_mechanism: Oncosuppressive sensor of aberrant mitosis and genomic instability
key_molecules: CDK1, Cyclin B, PLK1, Aurora kinases
overlaps: Overlaps with apoptosis and necrosis through cell cycle checkpoints and DNA damage.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: Oncosuppressive mechanism for the control of mitosis-incompetent cells by RCD or cellular senescence. Per se, mitotic catastrophe does not constitute a form or RCD
provenance_note: Keep distinct from mitotic death; it can culminate in more than one terminal death mode. [2]

operational_definition: Specific variant of RCD (most often, intrinsic apoptosis) driven by mitotic catastrophe
operational_definition_complement: A variant of regulated cell death driven by mitotic catastrophe, demarcated by delayed death following aberrant mitosis after radiation or drug exposure.
overlaps: mitotic catastrophe; apoptosis/necrosis downstream
galluzzi_nccd_definition: Specific variant of RCD (most often, intrinsic apoptosis) driven by mitotic catastrophe
provenance_note: Use as a broad mitosis-associated death bucket; retain mitotic catastrophe as a specific related label.

operational_definition: A lytic cell-death modality triggered by the synergism of innate-immune and metabolic signals, demarcated by BAX/BAK1/BID-dependent mitochondrial oxidative stress at the plasma membrane and culminating in membrane lysis.
overlaps: independent of pyroptosis/PANoptosis/necroptosis/ferroptosis/oxeiptosis
provenance_note: Candidate modality (G1+G2 passed; G2 by CRISPR/Cas9 Bax/Bak1/Bid triple-KO resistance, PMC12875127; distinct from MPT (CsA/CypD) and NLRP3); G5 replication pending; human.

operational_definition: Specific form of RCD triggered by perturbations of the intracellular microenvironment and relying on CYPD
operational_definition_complement: A regulated necrosis triggered by abrupt loss of inner-mitochondrial-membrane osmotic homeostasis via the permeability transition pore complex.
overlaps: downstream of MPT (Trigger)
galluzzi_nccd_definition: Specific form of RCD triggered by perturbations of the intracellular microenvironment and relying on CYPD
provenance_note: Canonical mechanism; see mitochondrial permeability transition for a synonym candidate. [2]

operational_definition: A modality of RCD triggered by perturbations of extracellular or intracellular homeostasis that critically depends on MLKL, RIPK3, and (at least in some settings) on the kinase activity of RIPK1
operational_definition_complement: Programmed necrosis regulated by RIPK1, RIPK3, and MLKL, leading to cell membrane rupture and inflammation. Programmed necrosis involving mitochondrial dysfunction and plasma membrane rupture induced by various stimuli.
core_mechanism: Programmed necrosis via RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL with plasma membrane rupture
overlaps: Shares signaling pathways with apoptosis and pyroptosis; can be activated when apoptosis is inhibited.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A modality of RCD triggered by perturbations of extracellular or intracellular homeostasis that critically depends on MLKL, RIPK3, and (at least in some settings) on the kinase activity of RIPK1
provenance_note: Independent mechanism within the regulated-necrosis umbrella. [2, 4]

operational_definition: Accidental and unregulated form of cell death resulting in cell lysis and inflammation. Programmed necrosis regulated by intracellular signal transduction pathways.
operational_definition_complement: A form of cell death demarcated by cell lysis and inflammation, encompassing accidental (unregulated) and programmed (signal-regulated) variants.
core_mechanism: Cell swelling, membrane rupture, release of cellular contents
overlaps: Accidental and unregulated form of cell death resulting in cell lysis and inflammation. Programmed necrosis regulated by intracellular signal transduction pathways.
provenance_note: Do not treat as a molecular RCD mechanism; map mechanistically resolved records to child modalities. [4]

operational_definition: A necrotic cell-death modality caused by sodium overload, executed via persistent activation of the TRPM4 cation channel by necrocide 1 (NC1).
overlaps: metalloptosis umbrella (sodium)
provenance_note: Candidate modality (G1+G2 passed); G5 replication pending; human TRPM4-specific.

operational_definition: A ROS-dependent modality of RCD restricted to cells of hematopoietic derivation and associated with NET extrusion
operational_definition_complement: Cell death involving the release of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) to trap and kill pathogens. Inflammatory cell death mode of neutrophils involving the release of NETs.
core_mechanism: Neutrophil death releasing neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)
overlaps: Involves the release of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), overlaps with pyroptosis and necroptosis.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A ROS-dependent modality of RCD restricted to cells of hematopoietic derivation and associated with NET extrusion
provenance_note: Retain as a distinct regulated-necrosis modality. [2, 4]

operational_definition: An accidental pattern of cell death (morphology) demarcated by cell swelling from failure of plasma-membrane ionic pumps, leading to necrosis with karyolysis.
overlaps: leads to necrosis; contrasts with apoptosis
provenance_note: Do not score as a discrete molecular mechanism.

operational_definition: Regulated form of cell death driven by oxidative stress and characterized by the involvement of KEAP1 and NRF2.
operational_definition_complement: A form of regulated cell death driven by oxidative stress, demarcated by KEAP1 and NRF2 involvement.
core_mechanism: Oxidative stress-driven, KEAP1/NRF2-dependent
overlaps: Similar to apoptosis and necroptosis, triggered by oxidative stress.
provenance_note: Retain as lesser-known distinct pathway; require form-specific assay criteria. [5] OD: AI-extracted from PDF corpus A (GPT-4o), human-validated.

operational_definition: An integrated inflammatory cell-death process engaging pyroptosis, apoptosis and necroptosis through the RIPK1/RIPK3-FADD-caspase-8 complex, orchestrated by ZBP1 and TAK1.
key_molecules: ZBP1, TAK1, RIPK1, RIPK3, FADD, caspase-8, NLRP3
overlaps: pyroptosis + apoptosis + necroptosis
provenance_note: Treat as an integrated program, not as a child of pyroptosis, apoptosis, or necroptosis.

operational_definition: Non-apoptotic cell death characterized by cytoplasmic vacuolation and lacking features of apoptosis. Non-apoptotic cell death involving cytoplasmic vacuolization.
operational_definition_complement: A non-apoptotic form of cell death demarcated by cytoplasmic vacuolation, lacking features of apoptosis.
core_mechanism: Non-apoptotic death with ER-derived cytoplasmic vacuolation
overlaps: Non-apoptotic cell death characterized by cytoplasmic vacuolation and lacking features of apoptosis.
provenance_note: Retain as a distinct non-apoptotic death label but apply form-specific evidence rules.

operational_definition: A modality of RCD initiated by PARP1 hyperactivation and precipitated by the consequent bioenergetic catastrophe coupled to AIF-dependent and MIF-dependent DNA degradation
operational_definition_complement: Form of cell death initiated by the hyperactivation of PARP enzymes leading to DNA fragmentation. Programmed death involving PARP-1 activation and AIF translocation to the nucleus.

overlaps: Mediated by PARP enzymes, overlaps with apoptosis in DNA damage response.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A modality of RCD initiated by PARP1 hyperactivation and precipitated by the consequent bioenergetic catastrophe coupled to AIF-dependent and MIF-dependent DNA degradation
provenance_note: Retain as an independently assessed RCD form. [2, 4]

operational_definition: A form of cell death caused by phagocytosis of viable cells, triggered by exposure of 'eat-me' signals or loss of 'don't-eat-me' signals.
overlaps: distinct from efferocytosis
provenance_note: Retain separately from efferocytosis; require source-level distinction between engulfment-driven death and clearance.

operational_definition: Particular form of RCD that occurs in strictly physiological scenarios, i.e., it does not relate to perturbations of homeostasis and hence does not occur in the context of failing adaptation to stress
operational_definition_complement: A genetically encoded, developmentally scheduled form of cell death, first defined from intersegmental-muscle degeneration during insect metamorphosis.
overlaps: parent of all programmed RCD forms
galluzzi_nccd_definition: Particular form of RCD that occurs in strictly physiological scenarios, i.e., it does not relate to perturbations of homeostasis and hence does not occur in the context of failing adaptation to stress
provenance_note: Do not score as a discrete mechanism; retain as a broad legacy label.

operational_definition: A necrosis-like inflammatory cell death of macrophages, executed in a caspase-1-independent manner via ASC and cathepsin B, with release of HMGB1.
overlaps: inflammasome components; caspase-1/IL-1b-independent
provenance_note: Retain separately; do not merge automatically with pyroptosis or regulated necrosis. [4]

operational_definition: A type of RCD that critically depends on the formation of plasma membrane pores by members of the gasdermin protein family, often (but not always) as a consequence of inflammatory caspase activation
operational_definition_complement: Inflammatory form of programmed cell death involving caspase-1 activation and gasdermin-mediated cell lysis. Programmed cell death associated with inflammatory response, primarily mediated by gasdermins.

overlaps: Overlaps with apoptosis and necroptosis; involves inflammatory caspases.
galluzzi_nccd_definition: A type of RCD that critically depends on the formation of plasma membrane pores by members of the gasdermin protein family, often (but not always) as a consequence of inflammatory caspase activation
provenance_note: Independent mechanism within the regulated-necrosis umbrella. [2, 4]

operational_definition: An umbrella term for genetically controlled, non-apoptotic necrotic cell death.
overlaps: parent of necroptosis/pyroptosis/MPT-driven necrosis
provenance_note: Aggregate-only category; do not score it as an independent mechanism. [4]

operational_definition: No single definition - Elicit-derived composite of senescence + autophagy in the cancer context.
reference_citation: Composite of Cellular senescence (NCCD_2018; PMID 29362479) + Autophagy (PMID 36864290) — composite pathway label, not a distinct NCCD entity
overlaps: senescence + autophagy (both defined)
provenance_note: WikiPathways pathway label (channel B) + Elicit_Phase3 (channel E); composite of Cellular senescence + Autophagy — NOT a distinct RCD entity. Retained per provenance policy P0/P1 (no deletion).

operational_definition: A programmed cell death of erythrocytes in which complement activation initiates (mini)NLRP3-caspase-8 complexes culminating in hemolysis.
overlaps: NLRP3-caspase-8 machinery in mature RBCs
provenance_note: Retain as supplied pending a frozen operational definition.

operational_definition: An endosome-dependent cell-death process (emerging concept).
overlaps: distinct from lysosome-dependent death
provenance_note: Retain as supplied pending a frozen operational definition.

operational_definition: A morphological, taxon-specific pattern of cell death demarcated by conspicuous cytoplasmic vacuolization; in the founding Dictyostelium discoideum (protist) study, autophagy-gene (atg1) disruption reveals a hidden non-vacuolar death pathway, indicating vacuolization is a phenotype rather than the execution mechanism.
reference_citation: Kosta et al. 2004 (Dictyostelium — name source; non-vacuolar pathway); plant context: Minina 2013 (PMID 24344187), Feng 2022 (PMID 35390283)
overlaps: autophagic vacuolar death
provenance_note: Treat as a morphology/context label unless a taxon-specific mechanism is provided. Expert adjudication (sentinel 2026-09): reclassified L4->L5 (TAXON); vacuolization is a phenotype, not a mechanism (atg1 disruption reveals a hidden non-vacuolar death); founding evidence Dictyostelium discoideum (protist); principal context plant (Norway spruce, Arabidopsis); not human.
species_scope: plant (Arabidopsis, Picea abies) + protist (Dictyostelium discoideum); not human
